facts.statement: Dalianraptor was similar to the avialian Jeholornis but possessed a longer thumb and shorter forelimbs, suggesting it may have been flightless.
facts.quote: Dalianraptor is very similar to the contemporary avialian Jeholornis, though it has a longer digit I (thumb-equivalent) and shorter forelimbs, which suggests it may have been flightless.

facts.statement: Dalianraptor reached a length of about 80 cm.
facts.quote: It also reached about 80 cm in length.

facts.statement: The holotype specimen D2139 was discovered before the 2000s and was initially labeled as a possible dromaeosaurid.
facts.quote: The holotype, D2139, was discovered sometime before the 2000s, when Matthew Martyniuk saw a photograph of the holotype, which was then labelled as an undescribed possible dromaeosaurid.

facts.statement: Researchers suspect the holotype might be a fossil trade chimera consisting of a Jeholornis body with arms from a flightless theropod.
facts.quote: More recently, it is being suspected that the specimen is a chimera forged for the fossil trade, namely a Jeholornis with the arms exchanged by those of an unnamed flightless theropod.

facts.statement: Dalianraptor lived in China approximately 120 million years ago during the early Cretaceous period.
facts.quote: El Dalianraptor (que significa "ladrón daliniano") es un género de ave prehistórica que vivió en China hace unos 120 millones de años, durante los primeros años del período cretáceo.

facts.statement: Fossils of Dalianraptor were found in the Jiufotang Formation in Liaoning province.
facts.quote: fue encontrado en las rocas de la Formación Jiufotang en la provincia de Liaoning.

facts.statement: Dalianraptor lived between 121.4 and 113.2 million years ago during the Aptian stage.
facts.quote: Time range: Aptian to Aptian (121.4 to 113.2 million years ago)

facts.statement: Dalianraptor is classified within the parent group Avialae.
Dalianraptor is classified under the class Reptilia.

rejected.statement: Dalianraptor is a dubious and possibly chimeric genus of theropod dinosaurs from the Jiufotang Formation in China.
rejected.quote: Dalianraptor (meaning "Dalian thief") is a dubious, possibly chimeric, genus of theropod dinosaurs from the Jiufotang Formation of China, dating to the Early Cretaceous.
